record_selection.scope: Kernel-module IRP handlers only; all six columns. External module PDBs are unavailable; default full-output comparisons remain failing and are recorded separately.

scope: Three full six-field defaults and three explicitly retained kernel-module scoped regressions; every reference symbol alias is compared. No five-field projection is used as parity evidence.
notes: Pinned SSDT.build_module_collection binds every SizedModule to the kernel symbol table. Native79 default DriverIrp now preserves this table domain, exact per-module RVA, all aliases and inclusive endpoints.

The earlier explanation that full parity required external driver PDBs described a different symbol model. Existing exact-PDB acquisition and dependency logic remains separately tested; default reference mode does not acquire those resources.
IRP labels attributed through the shared kernel table are reference algorithm observations, not proof of the external driver own debug symbol identity.
Reference-kernel-isf mode has no external PDB dependencies; cache validation recognizes that mode.

Native80 masks handler pointers in the native address domain and reads actual MmSystemRangeStart; only scalar read faults use the pinned default. Eight actual generator/pointer/helper vectors verify endpoints and high bits.
Native81 reads the direct NameInfo.Name.String chain without extra maximum/even-length or name-bit filtering; absent names are N/A and remain distinct from readable empty strings under mapping v2.
limitations: Native82 shares canonical tag-relative candidate recovery, padded optional headers, type maps and primary-layer ranges. Passing defaults still do not establish the complete damaged-header/paging and candidate-order contract.

Driver-name page-fault captures and the full shared-pool field-fault matrix still require review. MmSystemRangeStart and handler-pointer gates now have isolated actual fixed-generator vectors plus real defaults; all malformed scalar and architecture cases are not proven.
Half-open exact-PDB mode remains distinct from inclusive reference mode. Zero-size/overlap/naming behavior has synthetic reference vectors, not a complete malformed-module matrix.
Native partial diagnostic reporting is not identical to all reference debug logs or exceptions.
Other builds, architectures, damaged memory and full parameter/failure contracts remain unverified; complete plugin contract is not claimed.
Direct driver-name location/decoding now has synthetic reference vectors across four native descriptor modes; real name-field page-fault captures and malformed layouts still need broader validation.

vectors.scope: Actual SSDT build_module_collection and SizedModule/ModuleCollection queries. Synthetic loaded-module fields and a synthetic exact symbol-space query isolate shared table binding, aliases, names and endpoint behavior; no real driver names or PDB acquisition.

handler_vectors.scope: Actual kernel-space start, actual Pointer unmarshalling and actual DriverIrp generator. Synthetic driver/array/module collection isolates scalar gate, pointer domain, endpoint inclusion and continuation after one missing handler; not full pool/name/symbol behavior.

name_vectors.scope: Actual NameInfo property, DRIVER_OBJECT name method, UNICODE_STRING.String method and String constructor. Synthetic scalar/field adapter isolates location and decoding; native tests separately read physical/virtual descriptors on real fixture page tables. Does not validate pool carving or every NameInfo fault.

validation: Final native86 binary and unmodified fixed reference, real default/scoped cases compare all mapped fields and multiplicities. Historical cases not rerun retain their own per-case versions. Empty agreement is not positive evidence; no complete plugin contract is claimed.

driver_recovery.implementation: shared versioned pool ranges, tag-relative headers, padded carving and reference type map; eight readable DriverStart bytes, zero or strict masked threshold
driver_recovery.scope: Actual DriverScan.scan_drivers, builtin driver constraints and kernel-space-start helper. Synthetic carved objects/scanned-layer validity isolate eight-byte accessibility, pointer mask and strict DriverStart comparison. Does not prove full candidate recovery or name parsing.
driver_recovery.remaining: Header-field reads across scan-slice boundaries now have separate vectors. Tags split across ranges/chunks, layer overlap, malformed symbol tables, every missing-page boundary and other builds/architectures remain unverified.

tag_order_vectors.scope: Actual MultiStringScanner and PoolHeaderScanner, with synthetic decoded pool-header scalars. Tests address order across four-byte tags, constraint-order independence, non-overlap including rejected matches, binary patterns and empty buffers. Does not validate layer chunking, physical/virtual ranges, object carving or field read faults.
tag_order_vectors.implementation: merge one pending hit per four-byte pattern in scan-range address order, non-overlapping regex consumption; driver constraints share the same range read and global candidate cap
tag_order_vectors.remaining: Does not prove layer scan-chunk/overlap equivalence, boundary-spanning tags/headers, damaged-page coverage, or every plugin generator ordering.

header_boundary_vectors.scope: Actual PoolHeaderScanner plus actual pre-Vista/Vista pool predicates. Synthetic independent scalar reads isolate tag-only slices, partially external headers, unreadable unused tails and necessary fields. Native tests use real physical/virtual page tables and missing backing segments; these vectors do not prove layer scan chunking or tag discovery across slice boundaries.
header_boundary_vectors.implementation: BlockSize and PoolType are independently read from the scan slice when fully present, otherwise from the matching layer at the exact field address. Header prefix/unused tail do not need to be in the scan slice.
header_boundary_vectors.remaining: Does not prove discovery of tags split across ranges/chunks, scan overlap equivalence, all header layouts or damaged-page and resource-limit contracts.

chunk_vectors.scope: Actual DataLayerInterface/TranslationLayerInterface scan iterators and actual _scan_chunk/MultiStringScanner. Synthetic mapping ranges and read-fault adapter isolate chunk plans, overlap output suppression, data-layer tail repeats and continuation after failed chunks. Does not prove mapping enumeration, crash/hibernation decompression or full pool object carving.
chunk_vectors.implementation: 16 MiB chunk plus 4 KiB overlap, emit only tag starts below 16 MiB per chunk; actual data-layer versus translation-layer tail step; default physical maximum address excluded
chunk_vectors.remaining: Mapping enumeration, all backing formats, tags split across distinct mapping ranges, damaged-page/fault diagnostics and full plugin coverage remain unverified.
